text.p: Leg-spinner Ian Salisbury bowled his former county Sussex to defeat on Monday and earned Surrey a place in the Benson and Hedges Cup quarter-finals.
Salisbury bagged four wickets for four runs in six deliveries at The Oval as Sussex attempted to reach a 311 target.
Sussex, needing 55 off eight overs with seven wickets in hand, had a chance before Salisbury struck. In the end they failed by 11 runs.
Australian Tom Moody hit 92 for Worcestershire against holders Lancashire at Old Trafford but finished on the losing side.
Moody struck three sixes and 11 fours and added 131 for the second wicket with Graeme Hick. Hick contributed 40.
Worcestershire matched Lancashire's total of 274 for six with eight men down but were defeated because the hosts had lost fewer wickets.

In spite of the dramatic triumph, Lancashire's bid for a cup hat-trick failed. Their inferior run rate and Yorkshire's defeat of Minor Counties at Headingley left them out of contention in their qualifying group.
Yorkshire finished top by thrashing Minor Counties by 184 runs.
Anthony McGrath made a career-best 109 not out in Yorkshire's 309 for five. Their opponents folded for 125.
Northamptonshire reached the last eight helped by a five for 32 haul from off-spinner Jeremy Snape against Leicestershire at Northampton.
